study_type.claude: Mixed methods (literature review, interviews, questionnaire, qualitative system dynamics)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (literature review, semi-structured interviews, questionnaire, qualitative system dynamics/CLD)

research_method.claude: Literature review plus semi-structured interviews (12 key members, 4 companies) plus questionnaire on perceived factor strength (high/medium/low → 3/2/1, mean scores, Cronbach's α = .867 for 19 factors; 17 of 25 companies) plus qualitative system dynamics (influence diagram, CLD)
research_method.nlm: Literature review, semi-structured interviews (12 members, 4 companies), questionnaire (17 respondents, 1 per company, of 25 invited), qualitative system dynamics / causal loop diagram
research_method.value: Mixed methods: literature review to identify 38 factors; semi-structured interviews and face-to-face discussions with 12 key project members from 4 companies; questionnaire rating perceived influence strength (high/medium/low scored 3/2/1, mean-based selection of 19 factors, Cronbach's alpha) answered by 17 of 25 invited companies (one respondent each); qualitative system dynamics modelling (influence diagram and causal loop diagram)
research_method.note: Cronbach's α = .867 and the 38/19 factor counts reported by Claude only (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; Bangladeshi software companies using agile (100% Scrum) for at least 1 year, offshore and local markets; 12 interviewees, 17 questionnaire respondents
context.nlm: Industry; software companies in Bangladesh (offshore and local markets), 100% Scrum; 12 interviewees, 17 survey respondents
context.value: industry; Bangladeshi software companies using agile (all Scrum) for at least one year, serving offshore and local markets; 12 interviewees from 4 companies and 17 questionnaire respondents (one per company)

remote_covid.note: Both: work mode not specified; offshore clients and time-zone differences mentioned only in one interview remark.

data_window.note: Not stated by either. Full text reports data collected January–March 2017 (PDF p. 2).

cat_productivity.note: Claude tags the CLD 'actual team productivity' concept (not measured) and SLOC/function points (introduction, criticized) as Productivity. NotebookLM has no Productivity-tagged metric (output quantity tagged Activity). Productivity itself is only measured perceptually.

cat_quality.note: Quality is a management criterion for assessing team productivity; work quality and rework are CLD variables.

cat_collaboration.note: Communication (top-rated, 2.82), mutual trust and coordination appear as rated influence factors and 'communication & coordination overhead' as a CLD variable; neither extractor lists a collaboration measure. Author may wish to review.

cat_satisfaction.note: Both tag customer satisfaction (a management criterion) as Satisfaction, which is not developer satisfaction; developer motivation and exhaustion appear only as influence factors/CLD variables. Author may wish to review.

cat_activity.note: NotebookLM tags output quantity (SLOC/function points, a management criterion) and software reuse level as Activity; Claude has no activity metric. In the text, SLOC/FP appear only in the introduction.

cat_delivery.note: Timeliness as a management criterion for assessing productivity.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM's DevEx tag on staff turnover is generic; no DevEx framework.

cat_agile.note: Agile (Scrum) teams; adoption of agile practices/ceremonies (daily stand-up, retrospectives, release planning) reported from the survey.

cat_survey.note: Questionnaire on perceived influence strength of factors plus interviews on perceptions.

evidence.quote: A set of semistructured interviews and face-to-face discussions were also conducted with 12 key project members from 4 software companies including project managers, scrum masters, developers, project owners
a questionnaire [26] was developed and distributed to a total of 25 software companies in Bangladesh. Only 17 companies (1 from each) responded to the questionnaire.
The agile team members were asked to fill in the form to indicate the strength (high, medium or low) of the factors that they perceived influenced their productivity [25].
Cronbach's alpha coefficient for internal consistency reliability [21] was calculated for the selected factors
The complex interrelated structure of different factors affecting agile teamwork productivity is modeled using influence diagram and Causal Loop Diagram (CLD) for qualitative analysis.
companies using agile methods for at least 1 year and top listed companies developing software for both offshore and local market.
Although at the end of the project, the management assessed their productivity on the basis of timeliness and quality.
